To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the structure of the title complex, [Mg(DMFO)4(H2)2]Cl, has been redetermined at 113 (2) K, with improved precision, and that the crystal structure is stabilized by O—H⯤Cl hydrogen bonding.
the title compound crystallizes with two independent complex molecules, each with two aqua ligand molecules, in a monoclinic unit cell.
the crystal structure of the diaquatetrakis(dmf) magnesium dichloride has been redetermined at 113 K.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structural chemistry of magnesium complexes with DMF and related ligands, with particular attention to supramolecular interactions.
the crystal structures of metal complexes containing DMF as a ligand.
the synthesis, characterization and crystal structures of a variety of magnesium and calcium complexes with the dimethylformamide (DMF) ligand.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, at 298 K, the structure of the title complex is not well defined, whereas at 113  K it is.
the title compound is a pseudo-tetrahedral complex in which the two water ligands occupy axial sites of the Mg ion.
the structure of the title complex is a typical example of the well established Mg(DMF)6 octahedral coordination sphere.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Mg—O(w)—H⋯O hydrogen bonds, which are present in the title compound, are not strong enough to prevent the formation of the [Mg(H2O)6]2+ complex in water solutions.
the crystal structures of the title compound and its isomer, [Mg(DMFA)4(H2 O)2 ]Cl2 [DMFA is N,N-dimethylacetamide], are very similar.
the title compound has an almost idealized MgO6 octahedral geometry.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the absence of a crystallographically imposed inversion centre, a Mg atom is not constrained to be in an exact octahedral environment.

the crystallographic study of the title compound is a good example of the importance of the temperature at which a crystal structure is measured, as the geometry of a crystallographic structure depends not only on the nature of the crystal, but also on the temperature at which the crystal is studied.
